messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated KV page-in rate + continuous-batching regression detected in prod-us-west. Auto-severity: P1. Signals: sustained page-in spikes >900/s, token tail latency cliffs on long-context routes.
Priya: seeing block_manager churn across multiple hosts. Average block read latency up 6x. Memory pressure and io_wait spiking.
Jonah: verified perf cliff on routed-long-context: p99 token latency jumps to ~2.8s. Throughput backpressure causing queueing.
Omar: initial glance: block packing heuristic bumped to pack_factor=1.8 in last packing rollout, causing larger average block size -> expensive page-ins when metadata misses. Also a few hosts show duplicated metadata refs.
Lin: any customer visible failures?
Priya: a small subset of long-running sessions timed out (client-side 10s). Error rate bump ~0.6% globally, up to 2% for a high-traffic dedicated tenant. No data corruption.
oncall-bot: @oncall Jonah assigned.
Jonah: immediate plan: 1) isolate problematic hosts from serving (drain), 2) roll a conservative config to reduce continuous batching aggressiveness and disable prefix prefetch, 3) apply emergency block eviction mode to free memory faster.
Priya: preparing drain list and a temporary host exclusion tag: exclude.kv_paged=true. Will remove from load-balancer.
Omar: propose short-term config changes: `block_packing.max_block_size_mb=64`, `block_manager.eviction_target=0.6`, `continuous_batching.enabled=false` for long-context route group. Also disable `prefetch.prefixes=true`.
Lin: can we avoid full disable of continuous batching? That's heavy-handed. Maybe just reduce max_concurrent_batches and max_tokens_per_batch.
Jonah: prefer disable for targeted route group to stop the cascade. We'll do it for routed-long-context only; keep short-context routes running usual batching.
Priya: starting canary: applying config set to 3 hosts (us-west-gpu-4..6):
```
# canary config patch
continuous_batching:
  enabled: false
block_packing:
  max_block_size_mb: 64
block_manager:
  eviction_target: 0.6
prefetch:
  prefixes: false
```
deploy-bot: canary deploy started: infra/kv-paged-emergency v2026.4-canary -> us-west-gpu (hosts: 4,5,6).
Omar: also kicking off manual metadata sweep script on canary hosts to clear orphan refs: `tools/kv/metadata_sweep --mode=aggressive --concurrency=4 --dry-run=false` (running now).
Priya: logs from host us-west-gpu-5 during spike:
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:42Z] block_manager: read_block block_id=0x9f size=128MB latency=482ms
[2026-03-15T10:12:42Z] kv_index: lookup miss key_range=[0x8a..0x9f] refs=0
[2026-03-15T10:12:42Z] io: page-in 512ms retries=2
[2026-03-15T10:12:43Z] memory: rss=112GB page_faults=900/min
```
Omar: that block size 128MB is the problem; once metadata miss occurs, we pull a huge block. The packing rollout earlier prioritized fewer larger blocks; that was a regression risk.
Lin: canary metrics?
Jonah: after canary apply: page-in rate dropped ~70% on those hosts, p95 token latency for targeted route improved from 1.6s -> 320ms. CPU spikes from compaction observed but acceptable so far. Rolling to additional hosts in 10m.
Priya: I've notified Support: affected customers include two dedicated tenants (tenant-A, tenant-B). CSMs are being informed, escalation queued.
oncall-bot: Reminder: handoff in 20m to Omar for RCA.
Omar: working on two parallel actions: fast rollback of packing heuristic in staging -> test, and a code fix to metadata refcounting in the gc path. Found oddity: `metadata_index::dec_ref` not called in some error paths.
Jonah: mitigation checklist: 1) drain and exclude bad hosts, 2) deploy reduced block size and eviction config, 3) run metadata sweep, 4) targeted disable of continuous batching for long-context. Ensure we have rollback plan.
Priya: executing pool-level restrictions on non-critical workloads (embeddings batch jobs) to reduce contention: `quota.client:batch-embeddings=0.2` temporary.
Lin: thumbs up. Also enabling increased observability: `kv.metrics.refcount_histogram=true` and `block_manager.dump_on_eviction=true` for a short window.
Omar: extracted small repro from debug dump and pushed branch `fix/metadata-gc-2026` with a test that reproduces duplicate refs. Running CI now.
deploy-bot: rolling to 40% of us-west-gpu pool: infra/kv-paged-emergency v2026.4 -> in progress.
Priya: customer ops update draft: "We experienced intermittent elevated latencies/occasional timeouts for some long-context requests in us-west. We applied mitigations; targeted hosts are draining and configuration fixes are rolling. We will follow up with root cause and timeline for permanent fix."
Jonah: after second wave rollout to 40% pool, overall page-in rate down 62% vs peak, p99 token latency improved considerably. Still watching for metadata sweep side effects.
Omar: if metadata sweep triggers heavy IO, we may need to stagger it to avoid compaction-induced CPU spikes. Running sweep in 1-host increments now.
Lin: are we confident no customer data was evicted inadvertently?
Priya: manual checks show no user-visible data loss. Eviction policy is space reclaim; keys remain logically present in catalog. We'll include verification steps in postmortem.
oncall-bot: Handoff: Jonah -> Omar (timestamp handover).
Omar: taking ownership for RCA and patch. ETA for PR to fix metadata gc: ~2h for code + staging validation, then gradual deploy to prod next maintenance window or emergency release if needed.
Priya: summary for handoff doc to list: commands run, hosts drained, config diffs, links to debug dumps (s3://redwood-debug/2026/kv/pack-dump-1845006789.tar.gz), affected tenants, customer comms.
eng-shift-bot: incident log updated: ticket#INC-2026-3347 created and linked.
Jonah: thanks team. Keep this thread updated with any regressions.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations in progress; initial customer impact contained; severity remains P1 while metrics stabilize.
